picks.title: Maya 2026.2 lets you train your own AI animation models
picks.excerpt: Maya 2026.2's new 'Bring Your Own Data' feature lets studios train their own AI models for the MotionMaker animation system using their own keyframe or mocap data, moving generative animation from a black box toward a studio-tunable, in-house workflow.
picks.rationale: Highly actionable release — 'Bring Your Own Data' turns generative animation from a fixed black box into a studio-tunable, in-house model.

picks.title: Autodesk releases 3ds Max 2026.2 with editable Gaussian Splats
picks.excerpt: 3ds Max 2026.2 makes it possible to import, edit, relight and render 3D Gaussian Splat data directly inside the software, bringing radiance-field capture into a mainstream design/render pipeline alongside its other new features.
picks.rationale: Distinct release (not the earlier Houdini splat toolset) — editable radiance-field capture lands in a mainstream 3ds Max render pipeline; distinct accent since it shares the render category.

picks.title: I handed a UX review over to AI — here's what happened
picks.excerpt: A designer hands a full UX review over to AI and reports back: AI is a powerful partner for UX reviews but not a replacement for the expert, with accuracy coming from the domain expertise you feed it rather than the model itself.
picks.rationale: Concrete, tomorrow-usable account of AI-assisted UX reviews and where a designer's own expertise still has to lead; adds a new outlet and category.

picks.title: The screens are getting demoted
picks.excerpt: As AI grows more capable, the on-screen UI stops being the main focus of a product -- this piece reframes the designer's job around deciding which screens are still needed at all when interactions move to agents and ambient interfaces.
picks.rationale: Forward-looking reframe of the designer's role as interactions move to agents and ambient interfaces; distinct accent since it shares the workflow category.

picks.title: The art director's advantage in the AI-gen era
picks.excerpt: An art director argues the real edge in AI generative design workflows isn't better prompts or tools but trained visual judgment -- direction, taste and critique -- the human skills that decide whether AI output is usable.
picks.rationale: Third outlet plus a distinct angle — trained visual judgment, not prompting, as the durable human edge in gen-AI workflows; distinct accent since it shares the workflow category.
